newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Clark says Brash happy with wider target.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Clark says Brash happy with wider target.

text.p: New Zealand Labour Party leader Helen Clark said on Tuesday she believed Reserve Bank Governor Don Brash was comfortable with Labour's proposal to widen the target for underlying inflation to minus one to three percent from zero to two percent.

Clark told Reuters Financial Television in an interview: "I don't see the slightest difficulty with that. We've discussed it with Dr Brash in the past. He is well aware that the target range under which he operates is a very, very narrow one. I don't think he would have any difficulty with it if it was minus one to three (percent)."
Clark said in reply to a question she expected Brash to stay on as RBNZ governor if Labour won Saturday's general election.
Last month Brash said he could work with a slightly wider target band for underlying inflation than the current 0-2 percent range.
But he stressed the current band, defined in the policy targets agreement between the governor and Finance Minister Bill Birch, had served New Zealand well.
Brash said there was no perfect answer to what the width of the inflation target band should be.
"If it was slightly wider, I don't think it would necessarily be a resignation issue," Brash said.
"I think there are huge benefits in the present framework and I have yet to be persuaded a wider range would make sense.
"That is not to say it is not an issue which has to be looked at from time to time. Some wider bands I would feel very uncomfortable with, others might be looked at," he said.
"It would depend on the extent of it. It would depend also upon the mid-point of it."
